titleText.es: «Estooo, pues hemos hecho otra vez el estudio con las gominolas verdes y no nos sale ninguna relación. Seguramente solo fue una...» «CONTROVERSIA ENTRE LOS INVESTIGADORES SOBRE LA RELACIÓN ENTRE GOMINOLAS VERDES Y ACNÉ; ¡RECOMIENDAN MÁS INVESTIGACIÓN!»
titleText.en: 'So, uh, we did the green study again and got no link. It was probably a--' 'RESEARCH CONFLICTED ON GREEN JELLY BEAN/ACNE LINK; MORE STUDY RECOMMENDED!'
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd title attributes are preserved exactly. OCR split HALLADO, ENTRE, GOMINOLAS, VERDEAZULADO, CLARO, and RELACIONADAS across printed line wraps; those pieces remain single lexical occurrences. It misread PROVOCAN as PROVOVAN, omitted the gaming objection and newspaper subheadline, and partially recognized the repeated statistical notation. All twenty-one visible (P>0,05) labels, both game-name forms, NEWS, 95%, and 5% are audited exclusions. The Spanish raster visibly prints > in the green study too; the official raster has < there, so the localization error is documented and preserved rather than silently corrected.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Gominola is a common word in Spain for a small chewy sweet. In this comic, the colored pieces correspond to jelly beans.

example.en: We bought a bag of gummy sweets.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here provocar means to cause a result, not to taunt someone. Provocan is the present form for a plural subject.
Investigad is the positive command used with informal plural vosotros in Spain. It comes from investigar by replacing the final -r with -d.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we are (helping to describe an action in progress)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estamos is the present form of estar for nosotros. Before a form ending in -ando or -iendo, it helps present an action as ongoing.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: is left; ends up (in a resulting state)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here queda introduces the state that remains after something has been dealt with. The following completed-action form describes that result.
The color word rosa usually stays rosa in careful standard usage, but plural rosas is also widely used and is the form printed here.
Verdeazulado combines verde with azulado, describing a green shade that tends toward blue.

example.es: El agua tiene un tono verdeazulado.
example.en: The water has a blue-green shade.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The noun salmón is also used as a color label.
After a color, claro means a lighter shade.
Marengo names a very dark gray shade.

example.en: He is wearing a charcoal-gray suit.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The fruit name melocotón can be used as a color label.

example.es: Pintaron la pared de color melocotón.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In informal speech in Spain, ¡ala! can show surprise or amazement. This is unrelated to the noun ala, “wing.”

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Testing many colors separately makes it likely that at least one will appear linked to acne by chance; highlighting only that result turns random noise into a dramatic headline.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The strip illustrates the multiple-comparisons problem, often exploited through p-hacking: repeated tests create more chances for an apparently interesting result. In the official strip, the lone green result has P<0.05, the conventional threshold used to flag statistical significance. The Spanish raster mistakenly prints P>0,05 there as well as in the other twenty panels, and this source error is preserved. The newspaper then turns the selected result into misleading 95% reliability and 5% chance claims.
